question: Which schema and renderer contracts should HTML ingress and static output share, and which interactive dependencies can be removed?
trigger: The 2026-09-29 static-document execution left decoration reads at 21-58% of React time at 50 KB on S5 snapshot w, and left per-block decoration caching, which would need a declaration for document-reading sources, to its own decision. The user asked whether the proposed next steps (decoration read cost, per-block caching, the flaky schema benchmark, foreign-document placement and HTML leftovers) were the right target and what was missing.
requirements: A streamed preview costs work in proportion to what changed and stays equal to a fresh render.
Decorations keep the live editor's invalidation contract in live and static views: a read depends on its entry, the nodes inside it and state its source observes.
No mutable stable view; React Server Components keep working.
State that belongs to a live session (remote cursors, search matches, authored changes) never paints another document or static output.
evidenceReuse: Reused S5 snapshot w (summary-w.json and its per-source decoration split), the static reuse tests and the live decoration contract in Plite's decoration source and commit change keys. New: headless full-pass decoration timings on rich and CJK 50 KB documents; a headless stream through parseSlice({ partial, previous }) into EditorStatic's document at 10 KB and 50 KB; a seeded reuse oracle; and the S5 re-measure on the final tree.
summary: Pursue owner fixes and defer skipping unchanged blocks. The decoration cost came from sources reading everywhere and from a wrapper that trapped every property access, not from the live contract. Code highlighting now reads once per code block; the wrapper resolves its context once per view; document views find highlighting by block identity without indexing each document; previews render with useDeferredValue; and the registry previews render only when their document changes. On the final tree, React time per stream fell 48-55% at 10 KB and 73-74% at 50 KB against S5 snapshot w, and static source reads are 8-21% of React time. The browser still shows a pass over every top-level block, 1.7-3.8 ms per commit at 50 KB. Per-block caching and chunking are one decision, deferred until every source reads within its entry (the AI end marker reads the whole document) and static renders can see a version of observed state. The document views and block reuse reviewed on 2026-09-29 stand.

reconciliation.question: Which schema and renderer contracts should HTML ingress and static output share, and which interactive dependencies can be removed?
reconciliation.reason: Its block reuse, document views and guard stand. Its open limit, decorations read over every node on each render, is resolved by owner fixes, and per-block caching is deferred on browser evidence instead of being decided by a declaration.

alternatives: Per-block decoration caching behind a source declaration such as decorate.readsDocument. Defer: the per-block pass costs 1.7-3.8 ms per commit at 50 KB while every commit stays within the 32 ms cadence. A correct cache also needs sources that read only their entry and a version of observed state, and the AI end marker reads the whole document.

Chunked rendering, as Slate does for large documents. Defer, as part of the same decision: skipping an unchanged chunk is correct only under the same two conditions, it would save about 2-4 ms per commit at 50 KB, and it does not reduce style, layout or paint, which now grow more with size.
Memoize EditorStatic itself. Stop: re-rendering it is how a consumer refreshes decorations that read other state; consumers that re-render for unrelated state memoize the element on their document.

Delete static decorations and bake code tokens into the document at parse time, as HTML-producing Markdown renderers do. Stop: highlighting is paint, not content; baking it in forks static output from the live editor and bloats stored documents.
Keep per-text code highlighting with a text-level cache. Stop: the highlighter decorates a code block, and the live contract already re-reads an element whose text changed.
Throttle publications instead of deferring the render. Stop: a fixed interval idles a fast machine and still saturates a slow one; useDeferredValue adapts to the render's actual cost.
proofLimits: Browser numbers come from one Apple M5 Max in Chromium, S5 fixtures at 10 and 50 KB, at load 1.5-4.8. Static cells ran on run pp3 and AI cells on run pp4, which together are the final tree. Firefox, WebKit and documents beyond 50 KB were not measured. Only first-party sources were checked against the entry contract. Remaining size-dependent costs: the per-commit block pass (1.7-3.8 ms at 50 KB), static table cells that index each new document through table.read.cell (about 1.3 ms per commit at CJK 50 KB), the highlighter's type check through the plugin portal (0.2-0.55 ms per commit), and one end-of-stream restyle of the AI preview (90-136 ms at 50 KB). Global group-last/* utilities still restyle a whole subtree when a container's last-child state flips.
